rows.what the ink shows: The baseline has separate x, circled cross, and descending y beneath one straight outer bar. The short marks above x and y are heavily retraced into irregular hooks; their survival as bars versus cancellation is not secure.

A broad dark diagonal cross overlies a smaller rounded outline with a surviving lower arc. This may be a corrected tensor sign, but the ink alone does not securely distinguish replacement by times from heavy retracing of the circled cross.

After que there is a small detached hook, then a taller curved downstroke beside a short upright and two dots. The intervening letters of c’est and the accent/letter division in là are not individually secure at enlargement.

The left part is covered by a thick horizontal deletion; a short upward stroke survives near its start. At the right are an opening curved delimiter, crossed x-like strokes, a y-shaped descender and a closing curve, suggesting a canceled (x,y) expression rather than a terminal C; the preceding wording and exact allocation remain unresolved.

A large initial N survives, followed later by two neighboring tall stems and another tall/short pair above the deletion line. Nearly all connecting letter bodies and word boundaries lie in the cancellation, so the full proposed wording cannot be secured.

The canceled word retains an initial f with upper hook and lower return, compact upper arches across the middle, and a distinct dot above the i position before the final low group. These surviving components support fonction despite the covered baseline.

After fonction only an isolated tall stem, a low rounded rise and a short wavy terminal group survive above two long cancellation strokes. They do not securely identify the words or establish their divisions before the E expression.

After the baseline E there is a closed round outline with diagonal inner strokes rising above the two long cancellation lines. The visible upper diagonal arms support a tensor sign; the crossing centre is partly covered.

The upper deleted line retains an opening c-like hook, an upright t-like end to the first cluster, and a later p-shaped descender, compatible with “complet pour …”. Its heavy horizontal stroke conceals the intervening bodies and final words, so the full span cannot be securely recovered.

The lower deleted line begins with a tall curved, lower-looped stroke, but the following low letters and accents lie in the cancellation and do not securely distinguish “Séparé” from a different first word. The next word has the tall h/l group, dotted i and long ending of hilbertien.

After Notons, the low initial u/n strokes are followed by a narrow i, a descending q-shaped stroke, and the joined low uement sequence ending in an upturned t. The separated dots following it belong to the trailing ellipsis.

In the rotated margin, linéaire is readable in a small line above the horizontal deletion; the canceled band below has an upright initial and low ending compatible with another linéaire. The source placement between those two bands remains uncertain because the long horizontal stroke masks the lower letter bodies.

The continuation to the right of the canceled band has a looped a, low n, crossed tall t, dotted i, then a tall l and the remaining low néaire sequence. The diagonal paragraph cancellation crosses the word but leaves those identifying strokes visible.

The underlined marginal word has an open initial c, a connected low anon sequence, a separate i dot and a clear q descender before the final ue. The long line below is an underline; a separate diagonal cancellation crosses the middle letters.

The rotated margin has a tall d followed by an apostrophe and a low connected group with a descending p-like turn and terminal flat strokes. The cancellation crosses the start of this group but leaves the sequence compatible with d'espaces.

The last prose line ends with the shallow final stroke of d'espaces and remains blank to the margin edge; the diagonal strokes crossing that blank are cancellation lines, not another token. Directly below is display (3), beginning E'=, so no word corresponds to the existing illegible marker.

The first group has the initial tall curved stroke, an i dot and a final upright; the following close group has the humps and tall t strokes of maintenant. A large enclosing curve cuts through the first word and touches the latter group's end.

Following on, the word has a low initial trace, two conspicuous adjacent tall strokes for tt, and a short low ending. Those uprights and the final trailing stroke support mettra despite the abbreviated m/e.

The cancelled word begins with a small lower loop and upright d, followed by a small round remnant, a raised curved n-like stroke and a final rounded endpoint. The horizontal cancellation covers much of the baseline.

Before the gap, a shallow connected u/n/e group survives the strike; after it, the f has a tall stem and clear lower loop, followed by small rounded and hump remnants. The cancellation covers most of orme but the two-word grouping and looped f remain visible.

The opening short hooked bar supports on and the last connected low humps support une. Between them are several separated low strokes and a dot, but no secure word boundary distinguishes en connaît from a single compressed group, and the accent is not separately resolved.
